summary: Executed backend pytest API suite and end-to-end UI/admin integration tests on preview URL. Core flows work (landing load, 3D scroll scene, selector, enquiry submit, thank-you, admin CRUD content/leads), with one backend auth security gap and one notable responsive hero overlap issue.

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout did not trigger after 6 failed attempts (expected 429, received 401).

ui_bugs.issue: At mobile widths (confirmed 390px), top-left floating bead overlaps the main hero heading text area; at desktop there is close visual collision risk near left-side fine-print region.

issues: Decorative floating bead intrudes into title composition, violating non-overlap expectation

action_items: Fix auth lockout keying strategy: current identifier uses request.client.host, which changes across ingress nodes; use stable key (email + forwarded client fingerprint) so failed attempts aggregate correctly.
Tune hero floating bead positions/scales per breakpoint (especially <=600px) to prevent overlap with heading/fine-print copy.
Re-run backend brute-force security tests and responsive visual regression after fixes.
critical_code_review_comments: Auth lockout logic is vulnerable behind multi-node proxy because failed counts split by host IP; verified in Mongo login_attempts collection with two identifiers for same email.
CORS credentials behavior is correct with explicit origin and allow-credentials=true.
Admin seed password update path exists in startup logic; bcrypt hash format in DB is valid ($2b$ prefix).
No ObjectId serialization leakage observed in tested API responses.
seed_data_creation: Created and deleted TEST_UI_ lead via enquiry + admin delete; temporary admin content edit was restored to original.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest had 11 pass / 1 fail (lockout). UI flows validated: responsive widths 320/390/768/1024/1440/1920 with no horizontal scroll; bead selector verified 16/16 sources and keyboard nav; enquiry validation+submit to thank-you passed; admin redirect/login/leads delete/content edit+restore/logout passed.
rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout failure RCA: reproduction via repeated invalid logins showed all responses 401. Mongo inspection found same email split into multiple login_attempts docs keyed by different request.client.host values (e.g., 10.4.130.77:email count=4 and 10.4.130.138:email count=2). Because threshold check is per identifier, no single key reached lock threshold in time, so 429 never triggered. Mitigation: key by normalized email alone (or trusted X-Forwarded-For + email with stable parsing) and maintain atomic per-account/tenant lock counters.
